```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# **Non-filtered data is in the multisite_dataset_nonfiltered.csv file (no exclusion criteria applied, n = 1513)
  
# create vector of packages needed, load packages
# jmv is used for t-tests, correlations, anovas; TOSTER for equivalence testing; lme4 for mixed linear models
multisite_packages_rmd <- c("tidyverse", "jmv", "compute.es", "psych", "TOSTER", "citr", "lme4", "ggeffects", "ggplot2", "AICcmodavg", "knitr", "cocor", "Rmisc", "MBESS", "reghelper")
invisible(lapply(multisite_packages_rmd, library, character.only = TRUE))

source("spearman_ci.r") # used to calculate confidence intervals around Spearman's rho
source('task_scripts/calc_sdt.R') # used for SDT calculation

# dataset with no exclusions
multisite_dataset_nonfiltered <- read_csv("dataset/multisite_complete_dataset_nonfiltered.csv")

# dataset with no task data excluded, but demog/attention exclusion criteria applied
multisite_dataset_filtered <- filter(multisite_dataset_nonfiltered, failed_checks < 2, hearing_diagnosis != "Yes")

# this script applies the exclusion criteria for individual tasks 
# and creates the multisite_dataset tibble used throughout this script
source("task_scripts/filter_multisite_data.R")
                  
# separate dataframes for lab and online data
multisite_dataset_lab <- filter(multisite_dataset, origin == 1)
multisite_dataset_prolific <- filter(multisite_dataset, origin != 1)


# read CAPS and LSHS data by item, used for reliability analysis
CAPS_by_item <- read_csv("dataset/CAPS_by_item.csv")
LSHS_by_item <- read_csv("dataset/LSHS_by_item.csv")

attach(multisite_dataset)
```

```{r}
# calculate sample sizes and number of exclusions
total_n <- nrow(multisite_dataset_nonfiltered)
lab_n <- nrow(multisite_dataset_nonfiltered %>%  filter(origin == 1))
online_n <- total_n - lab_n
att_check_exclusions <- sum(multisite_dataset_nonfiltered$failed_checks > 1)
hearing_diagnosis_exclusion <- sum(multisite_dataset_nonfiltered$hearing_diagnosis == "Yes")
final_sample_n <- nrow(multisite_dataset)
final_lab_n <- nrow(multisite_dataset %>% filter(origin == 1))
final_online_n <- final_sample_n - final_lab_n

# number of participants at each data collection site (after exclusions)
n_by_site <- multisite_dataset %>% 
  group_by(site) %>% 
  tally()

```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
### Demographics and differences between lab/online samples ###

# calculate demographics - countries, gender, age, diagnoses
# Czech Rep was represented twice with different spellings - first line standardises this
multisite_dataset$country[country == "ÄŒeskÃ¡ republika"] <- "Czechia"
num_unique_countries <- length(unique(multisite_dataset$country))

# calculate proportions of genders (male, female, other, prefer not to say), and age statistics (mean, sd, min, max)
prop_female <- round((sum(multisite_dataset$gender == "Female", na.rm = TRUE)/final_sample_n)*100, 1)
prop_male <- round((sum(multisite_dataset$gender == "Male", na.rm = TRUE)/final_sample_n)*100, 1)
prop_other <- round((sum(multisite_dataset$gender == "Other", na.rm = TRUE)/final_sample_n)*100, 1)
prop_notsay <- round((sum(multisite_dataset$gender == "Prefer Not to Say", na.rm = TRUE)/final_sample_n)*100, 1)
mean_age <- round(mean(age), 1)
sd_age <- round(sd(age), 1)
min_age <- min(age)
max_age <- max(age)

# calculate age statistics for participants who took part in the lab (mean, sd, min, max, 95% CIs)
mean_age_lab <- round(mean(multisite_dataset_lab$age), 2)
sd_age_lab <- round(sd(multisite_dataset_lab$age), 2)
min_age_lab <- min(multisite_dataset_lab$age)
max_age_lab <- max(multisite_dataset_lab$age)
age_lab_ci_lo <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_lab$age))[3], 2)
age_lab_ci_hi <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_lab$age))[1], 2)

# calculate age statistics for participants who took part online (mean, sd, min, max, 95% CIs)
mean_age_prolific <- round(mean(multisite_dataset_prolific$age), 2)
sd_age_prolific <- round(sd(multisite_dataset_prolific$age), 2)
min_age_prolific <- min(multisite_dataset_prolific$age)
max_age_prolific <- max(multisite_dataset_prolific$age)
age_prolific_ci_lo <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_prolific$age))[3], 2)
age_prolific_ci_hi <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_prolific$age))[1], 2)

# t-test comparing age of lab-based vs. online participants, then assign effect size to variable
origin_age_ttest <- jmv::ttestIS(formula = age~origin,
                            data = multisite_dataset,
                            vars = age,
                            effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)
origin_age_es <- round(origin_age_ttest$ttest$asDF$`es[stud]`, 2)
origin_age_t <- round(origin_age_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat, 2)
origin_age_df <- origin_age_ttest$ttest$asDF$df
origin_age_p <- format.pval(origin_age_ttest$ttest$asDF$p, digits = 3, eps = .001)

# chi square test for association between gender and online/lab participation
# first, filters out participants who did not answer 'male' or 'female'
origin_gender_chisq <- filter(multisite_dataset, gender == "Male" | gender == "Female")
percent_female_lab <- round((sum(multisite_dataset_lab$gender == "Female")/final_lab_n)*100, 2)
percent_female_online <- round((sum(multisite_dataset_prolific$gender == "Female")/final_online_n)*100, 2)
origin_gender_chisq <- jmv::contTables(formula = ~ origin:gender,
                                  data = origin_gender_chisq,
                                  pcRow = TRUE)
origin_gender_chi_value <- round(origin_gender_chisq$chiSq$asDF$`value[chiSq]`, 2)
origin_gender_chi_df <- origin_gender_chisq$chiSq$asDF$df
origin_gender_chi_p <- format.pval(origin_gender_chisq$chiSq$asDF$p, digits = 3, eps = .001)

# chi square test for association between diagnosis and online/lab participation
# first, filters out participants who answered "Prefer not to say"
origin_diagnosis_chisq <- filter(multisite_dataset, diagnosis == "Yes" | diagnosis == "No")
percent_diagnosis_lab <- round((sum(multisite_dataset_lab$diagnosis == "Yes")/final_lab_n)*100, 2)
percent_diagnosis_online <- round((sum(multisite_dataset_prolific$diagnosis == "Yes")/final_online_n)*100, 2)
origin_diagnosis_chisq <- jmv::contTables(formula = ~ origin:diagnosis,
                                  data = origin_diagnosis_chisq,
                                  pcRow = TRUE)
origin_diagnosis_chi_value <- round(origin_diagnosis_chisq$chiSq$asDF$`value[chiSq]`, 2)
prop_diagnosis <- round((sum(multisite_dataset$diagnosis == "Yes")/final_sample_n)*100, 1)

# mean and CI for CAPS scores in the lab and online
mean_CAPS_lab <-  round(mean(multisite_dataset_lab$CAPS_total), 2)
CAPS_lab_ci_lo <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_lab$CAPS_total))[3], 2)
CAPS_lab_ci_hi <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_lab$CAPS_total))[1], 2)
mean_CAPS_prolific <-  round(mean(multisite_dataset_prolific$CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
CAPS_prolific_ci_lo <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_prolific$CAPS_total))[3], 2)
CAPS_prolific_ci_hi <- round(CI(na.omit(multisite_dataset_prolific$CAPS_total))[1], 2)

# t-test for CAPS score between lab and online participants
origin_CAPS_ttest <- ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~origin,
                            data = multisite_dataset,
                            vars = CAPS_total,
                            effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE, ci = TRUE)
origin_CAPS_t <- round(origin_CAPS_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat, 2)
origin_CAPS_df <- origin_CAPS_ttest$ttest$asDF$df
origin_CAPS_p <- format.pval(origin_CAPS_ttest$ttest$asDF$p, digits = 3, eps = .001)

```


```{r}
# number of cases excluded due to CAPS non-completion
CAPS_exclusions <- sum(is.na(multisite_dataset$CAPS_total))

# descriptive stats for CAPS (mean, sd, median, min, max, 95% CIs)
CAPS_mean <- round(mean(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
CAPS_sd <- round(sd(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
CAPS_mdn <- round(median(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE))
CAPS_min <- min(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE)
CAPS_max <- max(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE)
CAPS_ci_lo <- round(CI(na.omit(CAPS_total))["lower"], 2)
CAPS_ci_hi <- round(CI(na.omit(CAPS_total))["upper"], 2)

# descriptives table for CAPS, inc. skew and kurtosis
CAPS_descriptives <- jmv::descriptives(data = multisite_dataset, vars = CAPS_total, skew = TRUE, kurt = TRUE)
CAPS_skew <- round(CAPS_descriptives$descriptives$asDF$`CAPS_total[skew]`, 2)
CAPS_skew_se <- round(CAPS_descriptives$descriptives$asDF$`CAPS_total[seSkew]`, 2)
CAPS_kurtosis <- round(CAPS_descriptives$descriptives$asDF$`CAPS_total[kurt]`, 2)
CAPS_kurtosis_se <- round(CAPS_descriptives$descriptives$asDF$`CAPS_total[seKurt]`, 2)

# correlations between CAPS, age, and cigarette use, including 95% CIs
CAPS_demog_vars <- select(multisite_dataset, CAPS_total, age, cigarette_use)
CAPS_corr_demog <- psych::corr.test(CAPS_demog_vars, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
CAPS_age_corr_rho <- round(CAPS_corr_demog$r["CAPS_total", "age"], 3)
CAPS_age_corr_p <- format.pval(CAPS_corr_demog$p["CAPS_total", "age"], digits = 3, eps = .001)
CAPS_age_ci <- calc.Spearman.CIs(CAPS_age_corr_rho, n = CAPS_corr_demog$n["CAPS_total", "age"])
CAPS_age_ci_lo <- CAPS_age_ci$fiel[1]
CAPS_age_ci_hi <- CAPS_age_ci$fiel[2]
CAPS_cigarette_rho <- CAPS_corr_demog$r["CAPS_total", "cigarette_use"]
CAPS_cigarette_ci <- calc.Spearman.CIs(rs = CAPS_cigarette_rho, n = CAPS_corr_demog$n["CAPS_total", "cigarette_use"])
CAPS_cigarette_ci_lo <- round(CAPS_cigarette_ci$fiel[1], 2)
CAPS_cigarette_ci_hi <- round(CAPS_cigarette_ci$fiel[2], 2)

# create tibble with mean and sd CAPS score by gender, then conduct t-test and calculate 95% CIs
CAPS_by_gender <- dplyr::group_by(multisite_dataset, gender_bin) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(mean = round(mean(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                   sd = round(sd(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
CAPS_by_gender_ttest <- jmv::ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~gender_bin, data = multisite_dataset,
                                   vars = CAPS_total, effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)
CAPS_gender_d_ci <- ci.smd(CAPS_by_gender_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat, n.1 = CAPS_by_gender_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[1]`,
                           n.2 = CAPS_by_gender_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[2]`, conf.level = 0.95)

# t-test for CAPS score between right and left handed participants
CAPS_by_handedness_ttest <- jmv::ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~handedness_bin, data = multisite_dataset,
                                   vars = CAPS_total, effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)

# create tibble of mean/sd CAPS score by diagnosis and relative diagnosis, then t-tests between groups
CAPS_by_diagnosis <- dplyr::group_by(multisite_dataset, diagnosis) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(mean = round(mean(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                   sd = round(sd(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis <- dplyr::group_by(multisite_dataset, relative_diagnosis) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(mean = round(mean(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                   sd = round(sd(CAPS_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest <- filter(multisite_dataset, diagnosis != "Prefer not to say") 
CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest <- jmv::ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~diagnosis, data = CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest,
                                   vars = CAPS_total, effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)
CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest <- filter(multisite_dataset, relative_diagnosis != "Prefer not to say")
CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest <- jmv::ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~relative_diagnosis,
                                       data = CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest, vars = CAPS_total,
                                       effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)
CAPS_diagnosis_d_ci <- ci.smd(CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat,
                              n.1 = CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[1]`,
                              n.2 = CAPS_by_diagnosis_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[2]`,
                              conf.level = 0.95)
CAPS_rel_diagnosis_d_ci <- ci.smd(CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat,
                                  n.1 = CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[1]`,
                                  n.2 = CAPS_by_rel_diagnosis_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[2]`,
                                  conf.level = 0.95)

```


```{r}
# anova, CAPS score by cannabis use (5 levels), then compute 95% CIs around effect size
CAPS_by_cannabis_lm <- jmv::ANOVA(formula = CAPS_total~cannabis_use,
                             data = multisite_dataset,
                             effectSize = "partEta",
                             contrasts = list(
                               list(var = "cannabis_use", type = "polynomial")),
                             emMeans = ~ cannabis_use,
                             emmPlots = TRUE,
                             emmTables = TRUE)
CAPS_by_cannabis_polynomial <- as.data.frame(CAPS_by_cannabis_lm$contrasts[[1]])
CAPS_cannabis_ci <- ci.pvaf(F.value = CAPS_by_cannabis_lm$main$asDF$F[1],
        df.1 = CAPS_by_cannabis_lm$main$asDF$df[1],
        df.2 = CAPS_by_cannabis_lm$main$asDF$df[2],
        N = sum(multisite_dataset$cannabis_use >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        conf.level = .90)

# anova, CAPS score by alcohol use (5 levels), then compute 95% CIs around effect size
CAPS_by_alcohol_lm <- ANOVA(formula = CAPS_total~alcohol_use,
                             data = multisite_dataset,
                             effectSize = "partEta",
                             contrasts = list(
                               list(var = "alcohol_use", type = "polynomial")),
                             emMeans = ~ alcohol_use,
                             emmPlots = TRUE,
                             emmTables = TRUE)
CAPS_alcohol_eta <- CAPS_by_alcohol_lm$main$asDF$etaSqP[1]
CAPS_alcohol_ci <- ci.pvaf(F.value = CAPS_by_alcohol_lm$main$asDF$F[1],
        df.1 = CAPS_by_alcohol_lm$main$asDF$df[1],
        df.2 = CAPS_by_alcohol_lm$main$asDF$df[2],
        N = sum(multisite_dataset$alcohol_use >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        conf.level = .90)

# anova, CAPS score by parental income (5 levels), then compute 95% CIs around effect size
CAPS_by_ses_lm <- filter(multisite_dataset, ses != 0)
CAPS_by_ses_lm <- ANOVA(formula = CAPS_total~ses,
                        data = CAPS_by_ses_lm,
                        effectSize = "partEta",
                        contrasts = list(
                          list(var = "ses", type = "polynomial")),
                        emMeans = ~ ses,
                        emmPlots = TRUE,
                        emmTables = TRUE)
CAPS_ses_ci <- ci.pvaf(F.value = CAPS_by_ses_lm$main$asDF$F[1],
        df.1 = CAPS_by_ses_lm$main$asDF$df[1],
        df.2 = CAPS_by_ses_lm$main$asDF$df[2],
        N = sum(multisite_dataset$ses >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
        conf.level = .90)

# t-test, CAPS score by handedness, then compute 95% CIs around effect size
# handedness_bin refers to a variable where participants are grouped as right-handeded or non-right-handed
CAPS_by_handedness_ttest <- ttestIS(formula = CAPS_total~handedness_bin, data = multisite_dataset,
                                   vars = CAPS_total, effectSize = TRUE, desc = TRUE)
CAPS_handedness_d_ci <- ci.smd(CAPS_by_handedness_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat,
                               n.1 = CAPS_by_handedness_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[1]`,
                               n.2 = CAPS_by_handedness_ttest$desc$asDF$`num[2]`,
                               conf.level = 0.95)

# compute correlation between CAPS score and matrix reasoning performance
CAPS_mr_corr <- corr.test(CAPS_total, mr_score, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
CAPS_mr_rho <- CAPS_mr_corr$r
CAPS_mr_p <- CAPS_mr_corr$p
CAPS_mr_ci_lo <- round(CAPS_mr_corr$ci["lower"], 2)
CAPS_mr_ci_hi <- round(CAPS_mr_corr$ci["upper"], 2)

```


```{r echo=FALSE}
source("spearman_ci.r")

# calculate number of source memory exclusions due to high or low accuracy
smt_exclusions_hiacc <- sum(multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_overall_acc == 100)
smt_exclusions_lowacc <- sum(multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_overall_acc < 33.34)
smt_exclusions_oldnew <- sum(multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_oldnew_acc <= 50)
smt_exclusions <- sum(multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_overall_acc == 100 |
                        multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_overall_acc < 33.34 |
                        multisite_dataset_filtered$smt_oldnew_acc <= 50)

# select relevant source memory variables for analysis; separate tbls for lab-only and online-only data
smt_CAPS_LSHS_vars <- select(multisite_dataset, smt_imagine_hear, smt_misattribution_bias, smt_rm_acc,
                             smt_oldnew_sensitivity, CAPS_total, LSHS_total_score)

smt_CAPS_LSHS_vars_lab <- select(multisite_dataset_lab, smt_imagine_hear, smt_misattribution_bias, smt_rm_acc,
                                 smt_oldnew_sensitivity, CAPS_total, LSHS_total_score)

smt_CAPS_LSHS_vars_prolific <- select(multisite_dataset_prolific, smt_imagine_hear, smt_misattribution_bias, smt_rm_acc,
                                      smt_oldnew_sensitivity, CAPS_total, LSHS_total_score)

# compute means, standard deviations, ranges, 95% CIs, for source memory task variables, stored in tibbles for each variable
# smt_overall_acc refers to the overall percentages of correct responses on the task
smt_overall_desc <- round(tibble(mean = mean(smt_overall_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                 sd = sd(smt_overall_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                 min = min(smt_overall_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                 max = max(smt_overall_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                 ci_lo = CI(na.omit(smt_overall_acc), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                 ci_hi = CI(na.omit(smt_overall_acc), 0.95)[["upper"]]), 2)

# smt_rm_acc refers to the percentage of items correctly recalled as 'old', for which the source was also correctly recalled
smt_rm_acc_desc <- round(tibble(mean = mean(smt_rm_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                sd = sd(smt_rm_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                min = min(smt_rm_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                max = max(smt_rm_acc, na.rm = TRUE),
                                ci_lo = CI(na.omit(smt_rm_acc), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                ci_hi = CI(na.omit(smt_rm_acc), 0.95)[["upper"]]), 2)

# smt_oldnew_sensitivity refers to the no. of correctly recalled old items, minus the no. of new items misremembered as old
smt_oldnew_desc <- round(tibble(mean = mean(smt_oldnew_sensitivity, na.rm = TRUE),
                                sd = sd(smt_oldnew_sensitivity, na.rm = TRUE),
                                min = min(smt_oldnew_sensitivity, na.rm = TRUE),
                                max = max(smt_oldnew_sensitivity, na.rm = TRUE),
                                ci_lo = CI(na.omit(smt_oldnew_sensitivity), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                ci_hi = CI(na.omit(smt_oldnew_sensitivity), 0.95)[["upper"]]), 2)

# smt_imagine_hear refers to the number of imagined items incorrectly recalled as heard
smt_imagine_hear_desc <- round(tibble(mean = mean(smt_imagine_hear, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      sd = sd(smt_imagine_hear, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      min = min(smt_imagine_hear, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      max = max(smt_imagine_hear, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      ci_lo = CI(na.omit(smt_imagine_hear), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                      ci_hi = CI(na.omit(smt_imagine_hear), 0.95)[["upper"]]), 2)

# smt_hear_imagine refers to the number of heard items incorrectly recalled as imagined
smt_hear_imagine_desc <- round(tibble(mean = mean(smt_hear_imagine, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      sd = sd(smt_hear_imagine, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      min = min(smt_hear_imagine, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      max = max(smt_hear_imagine, na.rm = TRUE),
                                      ci_lo = CI(na.omit(smt_hear_imagine), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                      ci_hi = CI(na.omit(smt_hear_imagine), 0.95)[["upper"]]), 2)

# paired t-test between hear-imagine and imagine-to-hear errors
smt_errors_ttest <- jmv::ttestPS(data = multisite_dataset,
                            pairs = list(list(i1 = "smt_hear_imagine", i2 = "smt_imagine_hear")),
                            effectSize = TRUE, ci = TRUE)
smt_errors_t <- round(smt_errors_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat, 2)
smt_errors_df <- smt_errors_ttest$ttest$asDF$df
smt_errors_p <- format.pval(smt_errors_ttest$ttest$asDF$p, digits = 3, eps = .001)
smt_errors_d <- round(smt_errors_ttest$ttest$asDF$es, 2)

# create correlation matrix between source monitoring variables and CAPS total score, for whole sample, and lab data only
smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix <- psych::corr.test(smt_CAPS_LSHS_vars, method = "spearman", adjust = "none")
smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix_lab <- psych::corr.test(smt_CAPS_LSHS_vars_lab, method = "spearman", adjust = "none") 

# variable with correlation coefficient for correlation between imagine-hear errors and CAPS score
# then calculate 95% confidence intervals for Spearman's rho
# note that this calls the spearman_ci.r script (based on Bishara & Hittner, 2017)
# then format p value ready to be inserted into text
smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_rho <- round(smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$r["smt_imagine_hear", "CAPS_total"], 3)


smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_ci <- calc.Spearman.CIs(rs = smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$r["smt_imagine_hear", "CAPS_total"],
                  n = smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$n["smt_imagine_hear", "CAPS_total"])
smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_ci_lo <- round(smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_ci$fiel[1], 2)
smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_ci_hi <- round(smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_ci$fiel[2], 2)

smtimaginehear_CAPS_corr_p <- format.pval(smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$p["smt_imagine_hear", "CAPS_total"],
                                          digits = 3, eps = .001)

# calculate rho and confidence intervals for LSHS
smt_LSHS_rho <- round(smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$r["smt_imagine_hear", "LSHS_total_score"], 3)
smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_ci <- calc.Spearman.CIs(rs = smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$r["smt_imagine_hear", "LSHS_total_score"],
                                                 n = smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$n["smt_imagine_hear", "LSHS_total_score"])
smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_ci_lo <- round(smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_ci$fiel[1], 2)
smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_ci_hi <- round(smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_ci$fiel[2], 2)
smtimaginehear_LSHS_corr_p <- format.pval(smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$p["smt_imagine_hear", "LSHS_total_score"],
                                          digits = 3, eps = .001)

# conduct equivalence test (two one-sided t-tests) for imagine to hear errors
# to view plot within equivalence bounds, change 'plot' argument to TRUE

                                     r = smt_CAPS_LSHS_corr_matrix$r["smt_imagine_hear", "CAPS_total"],
                                     low_eqbound_r = -0.1, high_eqbound_r = 0.1, alpha = .05,
                                     plot = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
smt_CAPS_imagine_hear_equiv_p <- format.pval(smt_CAPS_imagine_hear_equiv$TOST_p2, digits = 3, eps = .001)
```

```{r warning=FALSE}
#centre and standardise each variable for use in LMM
multisite_dataset$age_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$age,

                                                center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$DASS_depression_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$DASS_depression,
                                                center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$DASS_stress_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$DASS_stress,
                                                center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$sdt_fa_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$sdt_fa,
                                          center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$dl_RE_sum_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$dl_RE_sum,
                                             center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$smt_imagine_hear_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$smt_imagine_hear,
                                                    center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
multisite_dataset$ds_mean_span_centred <- scale(multisite_dataset$ds_mean_span,
                                                center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)

#filter dataset to remove NA cases for each task
multisite_dataset_complete_cases <- filter(multisite_dataset, !is.na(age), !is.na(gender_bin),
                                           !is.na(sdt_fa), !is.na(dl_RE_sum), !is.na(smt_imagine_hear),
                                           !is.na(ds_mean_span), !is.na(ses))

# creates four models to predict CAPS total score, increasing in complexity, with site as a random effect
rand_eff_only_lmer <- lmer(CAPS_total ~ 1 + (1|site),
                      data = multisite_dataset_complete_cases, REML = FALSE)

baseline_lmer <- lmer(CAPS_total ~ age_centred + gender_bin + ses + (1|site),
                      data = multisite_dataset_complete_cases, REML = FALSE)

sdt_lmer <- lmer(CAPS_total ~ age_centred + gender_bin + ses+ sdt_fa_centred + (1|site),
                      data = multisite_dataset_complete_cases, REML = FALSE)

all_vars_lmer <- lmer(CAPS_total ~ age_centred + gender_bin + ses+ sdt_fa_centred + dl_RE_sum_centred +
                        smt_imagine_hear_centred + ds_mean_span_centred +
                        (1|site), data = multisite_dataset_complete_cases, REML = FALSE)



model_names <- c("Random effects only", "Baseline", "SDT only", "All task variables")
lme.models <- aictab(cand.set = list(rand_eff_only_lmer, baseline_lmer, sdt_lmer, all_vars_lmer), modnames = model_names)

# compares different models using anova, assigns p to variable for use in text
rand_baseline_comparison <- stats::anova(rand_eff_only_lmer, baseline_lmer)
rand_baseline_comparison_p <- rand_baseline_comparison$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]

baseline_sdt_comparison <- stats::anova(baseline_lmer, sdt_lmer)
baseline_sdt_comparison_p <- baseline_sdt_comparison$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]

sdt_allvars_comparison <- stats::anova(sdt_lmer, all_vars_lmer)
sdt_allvars_comparison_p <- sdt_allvars_comparison$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]

# calculate standardized coefficients and SE for fixed effects in model with all variables
all_vars_lmer_standardized <- reghelper::beta(all_vars_lmer)
```

# Exclusions based on pre-registered criteria
After applying preregistered exclusion criteria (failure of attention checks (*n* = `r att_check_exclusions`), diagnosed hearing impairments (*n* = `r hearing_diagnosis_exclusion`)), the final sample consisted of `r final_sample_n` participants (`r final_lab_n` in the lab, `r final_online_n` online) native to `r num_unique_countries` countries.

*CAPS* - A further `r CAPS_exclusions` participants were excluded based on a high number of missed responses to the CAPS scale (> 33%), or due to unfeasibly fast response to questions on the CAPS (< 1.5s per item).

*Source memory* - `r smt_exclusions` participants were excluded from the source memory data, meeting one or more of the pre-registered exclusion criteria: due to 100% task accuracy (*n* = `r smt_exclusions_hiacc`), scoring at or below 33.3% accuracy (*n* = `r smt_exclusions_lowacc`), or scoring at or below 50% on old-new accuracy (*n* = `r smt_exclusions_oldnew`).

*Dichotic listening* - `r dl_exclusions` participants were excluded from the dichotic listening task performance, based on Bless et al. (2015), due to scoring < 50% accuracy on homonymous trials in any of the three task conditions (*n* = `r dl_exclusions_homonym`) and/or scoring a laterality index of 100% to one ear (*n* = `r dl_exclusions_laterality`).

*Digit span* - `r ds_exclusions` participants were excluded from the backwards digit span data, scoring a mean span ≤ 3 (*n* = `r ds_exclusions_low`) or ≥ 12 (*n* = `r ds_exclusions_high`). One further participant was excluded because data from the digit span task did not save due to a technical error

*Auditory signal detection* - `r sdt_exclusions` participants were excluded from the auditory signal detection task data, scoring a \(d'\) of ≤ 0 (indicating at or below chance performance) (*n* = `r sdt_d_exclusions`), and/or a hit rate of ≤ 10% (*n* = `r sdt_hits_exclusions`).

*Adverse childhood experiences* - data on adverse childhood experiences was excluded if participants completed ≤ 66% of the questionnaire (*n* = `r ace_exclusions_missing`), or spent < 1.5s per item (*n* = `r ace_exclusions_timing`). In total, `r ace_exclusions` participants' data was excluded from the ACE.

------

# S4. Internal reliability of CAPS and LSHS-E
Internal reliability of the CAPS was good (Cronbach's $\alpha$ = `r CAPS_cronbach`), and comparable to Bell et al. (2006) and Bell et al. (2011), who reported $\alpha$ = .87 and $\alpha$ = .89, respectively. Similarly, internal reliability of the LSHS-E was good (Cronbach's $\alpha$ = `r LSHS_cronbach`), and comparable to Siddi et al. (2019), who reported $\alpha$ > 0.7 in a number of different samples.

------

# Source memory - further analysis
Exploratory (non-preregistered analysis) showed that there was a very small correlation between old-new accuracy and CAPS score (*rho* = `r smtoldnew_CAPS_corr_rho`, 95% CI = [`r smtoldnew_CAPS_corr_ci_lo`, `r smtoldnew_CAPS_corr_ci_hi`], *p* `r smtoldnew_CAPS_corr_p`), suggesting that increased reports of hallucinations were weakly associated with a higher performance on recognition memory. However, this association was not found when the LSHS-E was used as a measure of hallucinations (*rho* = `r smtoldnew_LSHS_corr_rho`, 95% CI = [`r smtoldnew_LSHS_corr_ci_lo`, `r smtoldnew_LSHS_corr_ci_hi`], *p* = `r smtoldnew_LSHS_corr_p`). Likewise, no other measure of source memory task performance correlated with LSHS-E score (all *rho*s < `r smt_LSHS_max_rho`, all *p*s > `r smt_LSHS_min_p`, uncorrected).  

------

```{r echo=FALSE}
                             dl_forcedleft_homonym_acc < 3 |
                             dl_forcedright_homonym_acc <3 |
                             abs(dl_laterality_index) == 1 |
                             abs(dl_forced_left_index) == 1 |
                             abs(dl_forced_right_index) == 1))

# select variables for correlation matrix, all data
dl_CAPS_LSHS_vars <- select(multisite_dataset, dl_RE_sum, dl_RE_forcedright_sum, dl_LE_forcedleft_sum,
                            CAPS_total, LSHS_total_score, SPQ_cp, SPQ_do, SPQ_ip)

# select variables for correlation matrix, lab-only data
dl_CAPS_LSHS_vars_lab <- select(multisite_dataset_lab, dl_RE_sum, dl_RE_forcedright_sum, dl_LE_forcedleft_sum,
                                CAPS_total, LSHS_total_score, SPQ_cp, SPQ_do, SPQ_ip)

# non-forced condition, descriptive stats
dl_nf_descriptives <- round(tibble(RE_nf_mean = mean(dl_RE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_nf_sd = sd(dl_RE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_nf_min = min(dl_RE_sum, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                   RE_nf_max = max(dl_RE_sum, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                   RE_nf_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   RE_nf_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   LE_nf_mean = mean(dl_LE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_nf_sd = sd(dl_LE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_nf_min = min(dl_LE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_nf_max = max(dl_LE_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_nf_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   LE_nf_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   index_nf_mean = mean(dl_laterality_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_nf_sd = sd(dl_laterality_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_nf_min = min(dl_laterality_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_nf_max = max(dl_laterality_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_nf_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_laterality_index), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   index_nf_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_laterality_index), 0.95)[["upper"]]),2)


# forced-right condition, descriptive stats
dl_fr_descriptives <- round(tibble(RE_fr_mean = mean(dl_RE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fr_sd = sd(dl_RE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fr_min = min(dl_RE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fr_max = max(dl_RE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fr_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_forcedright_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   RE_fr_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_forcedright_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   LE_fr_mean = mean(dl_LE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fr_sd = sd(dl_LE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fr_min = min(dl_LE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fr_max = max(dl_LE_forcedright_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fr_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_forcedright_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   LE_fr_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_forcedright_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   index_fr_mean = mean(dl_forced_right_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fr_sd = sd(dl_forced_right_index, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                   index_fr_min = min(dl_forced_right_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fr_max = max(dl_forced_right_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fr_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_forced_right_index), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   index_fr_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_forced_right_index), 0.95)[["upper"]]),2)

#forced-left condition, descriptive stats
dl_fl_descriptives <- round(tibble(RE_fl_mean = mean(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fl_sd = sd(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fl_min = min(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fl_max = max(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   RE_fl_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   RE_fl_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_RE_forcedleft_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   LE_fl_mean = mean(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fl_sd = sd(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fl_min = min(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fl_max = max(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   LE_fl_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   LE_fl_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_LE_forcedleft_sum), 0.95)[["upper"]],
                                   index_fl_mean = mean(dl_forced_left_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fl_sd = sd(dl_forced_left_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fl_min = min(dl_forced_left_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fl_max = max(dl_forced_left_index, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   index_fl_ci_lo = CI(na.omit(dl_forced_left_index), 0.95)[["lower"]],
                                   index_fl_ci_hi = CI(na.omit(dl_forced_left_index), 0.95)[["upper"]]),2)

# paired t-test between right and left ear correct responses in the three conditions, and laterality index in each forced condition, competed to non-forced condition
dl_ttest <- ttestPS(data = multisite_dataset,
                    pairs = list(
                      list(i1 = "dl_RE_sum", i2 = "dl_LE_sum"),
                      list(i1 = "dl_RE_forcedright_sum", i2 = "dl_LE_forcedright_sum"),
                      list(i1 = "dl_RE_forcedleft_sum", i2 = "dl_LE_forcedleft_sum"),
                      list(i1 = "dl_forced_right_index", i2 = "dl_laterality_index"),
                      list(i1 = "dl_forced_left_index", i2 = "dl_laterality_index")),
                    effectSize = TRUE, ci = TRUE, desc = TRUE)

# create variables for individual t-test statistics to insert easily into text
dl_ttest_nf_df <- dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[1]
dl_ttest_nf_t <- round((dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[1]), 2)
dl_ttest_nf_p <- format.pval((dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[1]), digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_nf_d <- round((dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[1]), 2)

dl_ttest_fr_df <- dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[2]
dl_ttest_fr_t <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[2], 2)
dl_ttest_fr_p <- format.pval(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[2], digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_fr_d <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[2], 2)

dl_ttest_frindex_df <- dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[4]
dl_ttest_frindex_t <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[4], 2)
dl_ttest_frindex_p <- format.pval(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[4], digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_frindex_d <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[4], 2)

dl_ttest_fl_df <- dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[3]
dl_ttest_fl_t <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[3], 2)
dl_ttest_fl_p <- format.pval(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[3], digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_fl_d <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[3], 2)

dl_ttest_flindex_df <- dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[5]
dl_ttest_flindex_t <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[5], 2)
dl_ttest_flindex_p <- format.pval(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[5], digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_flindex_d <- round(dl_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[5], 2)

# one-sample t-test to test whether non-forced laterality index is different to 0
dl_index_ttest <- ttestOneS(data = multisite_dataset,
                            vars = vars(dl_laterality_index, dl_forced_right_index, dl_forced_left_index), 
                            effectSize = TRUE, ci = TRUE, desc = TRUE)

dl_ttest_nfindex_df <- dl_index_ttest$ttest$asDF$df[1]
dl_ttest_nfindex_t <- round(dl_index_ttest$ttest$asDF$stat[1], 2)
dl_ttest_nfindex_p <- format.pval(dl_index_ttest$ttest$asDF$p[1], digits = 3, eps = .001)
dl_ttest_nfindex_d <- round(dl_index_ttest$ttest$asDF$es[1], 2)
```

# Dichotic listening - task performance analysis
In the non-forced attention condition, as expected an overall right ear advantage was evident; that is, participants were more likely to correctly identify the syllable presented to their right ear (*M* = `r dl_nf_descriptives$RE_nf_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_nf_descriptives$RE_nf_ci_lo`, `r dl_nf_descriptives$RE_nf_ci_hi`]) than the syllable presented to their left ear (*M* = `r dl_nf_descriptives$LE_nf_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_nf_descriptives$LE_nf_ci_lo`, `r dl_nf_descriptives$LE_nf_ci_hi`]) (*t*(`r dl_ttest_nf_df`) = `r dl_ttest_nf_t`, *p* `r dl_ttest_nf_p`, *d* = `r dl_ttest_nf_d`), resulting in a laterality index significantly different from 0 across the whole sample (*M* = `r dl_nf_descriptives$index_nf_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_nf_descriptives$index_nf_ci_lo`, `r dl_nf_descriptives$index_nf_ci_hi`], *t*(`r dl_ttest_nfindex_df`) = `r dl_ttest_nfindex_t`, *p* `r dl_ttest_nfindex_p`, *d* = `r dl_ttest_nfindex_d`). In the forced right condition, participants were more likely to correctly report the syllable presented to their right ear (*M* = `r dl_fr_descriptives$RE_fr_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_fr_descriptives$RE_fr_ci_lo`, `r dl_fr_descriptives$RE_fr_ci_hi`]) than the syllable presented to their left ear (*M* = `r dl_fr_descriptives$LE_fr_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_fr_descriptives$LE_fr_ci_lo`, `r dl_fr_descriptives$LE_fr_ci_hi`]) (*t*(`r dl_ttest_fr_df`) = `r dl_ttest_fr_t`, p `r dl_ttest_fr_p`, d = `r dl_ttest_fr_d`). The laterality index in the forced right condition (*M* = `r dl_fr_descriptives$index_fr_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_fr_descriptives$index_fr_ci_lo`, `r dl_fr_descriptives$index_fr_ci_hi`]) was significantly higher than in the non-forced condition (*t*(`r dl_ttest_frindex_df`) = `r dl_ttest_frindex_t`, *p* `r dl_ttest_frindex_p`, *d* = `r dl_ttest_frindex_d`), indicating successful orienting of attention towards the right ear, across the whole sample. In the forced left condition, participants were more likely to correctly report the syllable presented to the left ear (*M* = `r dl_fl_descriptives$LE_fl_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_fl_descriptives$LE_fl_ci_lo`, `r dl_fl_descriptives$LE_fl_ci_hi`]) than the syllable presented to the right ear (*M* = `r dl_fl_descriptives$RE_fl_mean`, 95% CI = [`r dl_fl_descriptives$RE_fl_ci_lo`, `r dl_fl_descriptives$RE_fl_ci_hi`]) (*t*(`r dl_ttest_fl_df`) = `r dl_ttest_fl_t`, *p* `r dl_ttest_fl_p`, *d* = `r dl_ttest_fl_d`). The laterality index in the forced left condition (*M* = `r dl_fl_descriptives$index_fl_mean`, 95% CI = `r dl_fl_descriptives$index_fl_ci_lo`, `r dl_fl_descriptives$index_fl_ci_hi`) was lower than in the non-forced condition (t(`r dl_ttest_flindex_df`) = `r dl_ttest_flindex_t`, *p* `r dl_ttest_flindex_p`, *d* = `r dl_ttest_flindex_d`), indicating successful orientation of attention towards the left ear across the whole sample, as expected.
